$comment: Template: one ticket-lifecycle event. Append-only — events are NEVER edited or deleted.
One file per event, deliberately: two files with different names can never conflict in git,
so five people and three agents all push freely with zero merge resolution. A single shared
JSONL would conflict on its last line. Directories are cheap; conflicts are not.
Emitted by CI from signals that already exist (branch pushed, PR opened, review submitted, PR
merged) — never by a human pressing a button. Data that is a byproduct of the work is
accurate; data that is a report about the work drifts.
The backlog and the done archive become GENERATED views over ticket content + these events.
Nobody hand-edits them, which removes both the merge-conflict class and convention decay.
Stream id is <project>/<ticketId>, which is why ticket ids stay short and unprefixed: the
project is the partition, not a string prefix on every id.
type: drafted | content-synced | admitted | claimed | released | pr-opened | reviewed
